claims.claim: Voice is built into the standard promptarena binary; no special build is needed
The mic stays open the whole session and speaker audio feeds back into the mic without headphones, causing echo loops
An Arena config needs at least one provider and one agent declared to start a voice session
The promptarena binary stays pure Go with no cgo
The binary loads PortAudio dynamically at runtime, and only when a voice session starts
npm install -g @altairalabs/promptarena installs the promptarena CLI
go build -o bin/promptarena ./arena/cmd/promptarena builds the CLI
chat --voice without PortAudio prints a clear install hint and every other feature keeps working
On macOS, PortAudio is installed with: brew install portaudio
On Debian / Ubuntu, PortAudio is installed with: sudo apt install libportaudio2
On Fedora / RHEL, PortAudio is installed with: sudo dnf install portaudio
On Windows, portaudio.dll must be placed on PATH
Example command: promptarena chat --voice --config config.arena.yaml
The voice console opens in full-screen TUI mode
The agent responds with synthesized audio
Pressing q or Ctrl-C exits the voice console
OpenAI Realtime and Gemini Live handle turn detection natively inside the connection
ASM streams raw PCM from the microphone directly into the provider connection, and the provider signals when a turn is complete
ASM mode is the default for realtime providers
ASM is selected automatically for any provider that supports stream input, with no extra flags
The audio_enabled: true provider setting enables stream input
The response_modalities: [AUDIO] setting enables stream input
Standard chat-completion providers without streaming audio input fall back to client-side VAD
In VAD mode the mic is recorded locally until silence is detected, then transcribed via an STT provider and sent as a text turn
In VAD mode, TTS converts the agent's reply to audio for playback
Example command: promptarena chat --voice --voice-stt openai-whisper --voice-output-voice alloy --config config.arena.yaml
The --voice-stt flag exists and takes an STT provider id
The --voice-output-voice flag exists and takes a TTS voice id
--voice-stt must match a provider declared under stt_providers: in the Arena config
--voice-output-voice must match a voice id declared under voices: in the Arena config
The value of --voice-output-voice is a voice binding id, the id: field of an entry in the voices: list, not a raw vendor voice name
The voice binding maps the id to the actual synthesis voice for the configured provider
The --echo-guard flag exists and gates the mic while the agent is speaking
Example command: promptarena chat --voice --echo-guard --config config.arena.yaml
Echo guard is off by default
Echo guard adds a small latency
Echo guard is best-effort in v1: it suppresses capture during playback but does not perform full acoustic echo cancellation
Headphones give the lowest latency and cleanest transcription compared with echo guard
The --voice flag defaults to false
The --voice flag requires PortAudio installed
The --voice-stt flag has no default and is the STT provider id for VAD mode
The --voice-output-voice flag has no default and is the TTS voice id used in VAD mode
The --echo-guard flag defaults to false
The --config flag defaults to config.arena.yaml
The --config flag exists and takes the path to the Arena config file
